from manim import *
import random

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        title = "The Mystery of Predictable Chaos"
        lines = [
            "Welcome to the world of unpredictable and chaotic data.",
            "Imagine a forest filled with giant, oddly weighted squirrels.",
            "Individual weights are messy, following no specific pattern."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Squirrel colors and attributes
        SQUIRREL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create 15 squirrel representatives (circles of varying sizes)
        squirrels = VGroup()
        grid_spots = [
            'B1', 'B3', 'B5', 'C2', 'C4', 'C6', 
            'D1', 'D3', 'D5', 'E2', 'E4', 'E6',
            'F1', 'F3', 'F5'
        ]
        
        for i in range(15):
            # Size ranges from 1kg to 20kg (scaled for visibility)
            weight = random.uniform(1, 20)
            radius = 0.05 + (weight / 20) * 0.15
            sq = Circle(radius=radius, fill_opacity=0.8, color=SQUIRREL_COLOR, fill_color=SQUIRREL_COLOR)
            self.place_at_grid(sq, grid_spots[i])
            squirrels.add(sq)
            
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(SQUIRREL_COLOR),
            FadeIn(squirrels, shift=UP),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line, subtly jiggle squirrels to represent chaotic nature
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SQUIRREL_COLOR),
            *[sq.animate.shift(np.array([random.uniform(-0.1, 0.1), random.uniform(-0.1, 0.1), 0])) for sq in squirrels],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to a flat histogram arrangement
        # Create a basic number line at the bottom
        axis = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 20, 5],
            length=5,
            color=WHITE,
            include_numbers=True,
            font_size=18,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        self.place_in_area(axis, 'F1', 'F6')
        
        # Target positions for flat histogram (spread along the axis)
        # We simulate "flat" by spreading them linearly across the x-range
        target_positions = []
        axis_start = axis.n2p(0)
        axis_end = axis.n2p(20)
        
        for i in range(15):
            # Linearly distribute to show no peak/bell curve
            pos_x = axis_start[0] + (i / 14) * (axis_end[0] - axis_start[0])
            target_positions.append(np.array([pos_x, axis_start[1] + 0.3, 0]))

        # Highlight one specific squirrel
        target_squirrel = squirrels[7]
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR),
            Create(axis),
            *[squirrels[i].animate.move_to(target_positions[i]) for i in range(15)],
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Place question mark above the highlighted squirrel
        question_mark.next_to(target_squirrel, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            target_squirrel.animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR).set_fill(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR),
            Write(question_mark),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's define our population: a bag of diverse marbles.",
            "A sample is just a small scoop from that bag.",
            "The sample mean represents the average of that scoop."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Kit: Populations and Samples", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Match lecture color and highlight line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create Population Container (visualizing the bag)
        # Using area A2 to D5
        container = RoundedRectangle(
            width=4.0, height=3.5, corner_radius=0.3, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=3
        )
        self.place_in_area(container, "A2", "D5")
        
        pop_label = Text("Population", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(pop_label, "A2").shift(UP * 0.4)

        # Fill with 100 diverse "marbles" (Dots)
        marbles = VGroup()
        colors = [RED_A, BLUE_A, YELLOW_A, GREEN_A, PINK, ORANGE, PURPLE_A, WHITE]
        random.seed(42)
        for _ in range(100):
            # Coordinates range roughly A2(1.5, 2.2) to D5(4.5, -0.8)
            rx = random.uniform(1.7, 4.3)
            ry = random.uniform(-0.6, 2.0)
            dot = Dot(point=[rx, ry, 0], radius=0.06, color=random.choice(colors))
            marbles.add(dot)

        self.play(Create(container), Write(pop_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(marbles, lag_ratio=0.005), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Change color of lecture line 2 to green
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Select 5 marbles for the scoop
        sample_indices = [15, 32, 45, 78, 92]
        sample_marbles = VGroup(*[marbles[i] for i in sample_indices])
        
        # Visual green scoop (circle selection)
        scoop_circle = Circle(radius=0.7, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        scoop_circle.move_to(sample_marbles.get_center())

        self.play(Create(scoop_circle))
        self.play(sample_marbles.animate.set_color("#00FF00").scale(1.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Change color of lecture line 3 to yellow
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Move the selected sample to the side area (E3)
        sample_move_group = VGroup(scoop_circle, sample_marbles)
        target_pos = self.grid["E3"]
        
        sample_label = Text("Sample", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(sample_label, "E2").shift(LEFT * 0.4)
        
        # Mean calculation display
        mean_label = Text("Sample Mean:", font_size=22, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(mean_label, "F3").shift(LEFT * 0.9)
        
        mean_val = DecimalNumber(0.0, num_decimal_places=1, color="#FFFF00", mob_class=Text)
        self.place_at_grid(mean_val, "F3").shift(RIGHT * 1.1)

        self.play(
            sample_move_group.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            FadeIn(sample_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Display the result of the 'scoop'
        self.play(
            Write(mean_label),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(mean_val, 14.8),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            'The Central Limit Theorem reveals a hidden mathematical law.', 
            'As sample size grows, the distribution shape transforms.', 
            'Uniform or skewed data eventually yields a bell curve.', 
            'This normal distribution is symmetrical and highly predictable.', 
            'Large samples always find order within the original mess.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Reveal: The Bell Curve Emerges", lines)
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#FFFF00", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF", "#FF00FF", "#FFFFFF"]

        # === Asset Preparation ===

        # 1. Skewed Population Distribution (Preview)
        # Positioned at A4-B6
        pop_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 1},
            x_length=2.5, y_length=1.5
        ).set_color(GRAY_C)
        
        # A skewed curve: Gamma-like 4*x*exp(-2x)
        pop_curve = pop_axes.plot(lambda x: 4 * x * np.exp(-2 * x), x_range=[0, 5], color=YELLOW)
        pop_label = Text("Skewed Population", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(pop_axes, UP, buff=0.1)
        pop_group = VGroup(pop_axes, pop_curve, pop_label)
        self.place_in_area(pop_group, "A4", "B6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # 2. Sampling Distribution Main Axes
        # Positioned at C1-F6
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False},
            x_length=5.5, y_length=3.0
        ).set_color(WHITE)
        
        axes_labels = VGroup(
            Text("Sample Mean", font_size=16).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN),
            Text("Freq", font_size=16).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT)
        )
        main_axes_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        self.place_in_area(main_axes_group, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)

        # 3. Dynamic Histogram Setup
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        num_bars = 20
        bar_width = 5.0 / num_bars
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(
                width=bar_width * 0.8, height=0.1, 
                fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=0.5
            ) for _ in range(num_bars)
        ])

        def update_histogram(mob):
            n = n_tracker.get_value()
            alpha = np.clip((n - 2) / 28.0, 0, 1) # Transition factor from 2 to 30
            
            for i, bar in enumerate(mob):
                # Map index to x in range [-2.5, 2.5]
                x = -2.5 + i * (5.0 / (num_bars - 1))
                
                # Skewed component (shifted and scaled)
                skew_val = max(0, (x + 1.2) * np.exp(-(x + 1.2)) * 3.5)
                # Normal component
                norm_val = np.exp(-(x**2) / (2 * 0.6**2)) * 1.2
                
                # Combined height
                h = (1 - alpha) * skew_val + alpha * norm_val
                
                bar.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.05, h))
                bar.move_to(axes.c2p(x, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)

        bars.add_updater(update_histogram)

        # 4. n-Value Indicator
        n_label = Text("Sample Size n =", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        n_val_text = Text("2", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        n_display = VGroup(n_label, n_val_text).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(n_display, "C1", scale_factor=1.0)

        def update_n_text(mob):
            val = int(n_tracker.get_value())
            new_mob = Text(str(val), font_size=20, color=GREEN)
            mob.become(new_mob.move_to(mob))
        n_val_text.add_updater(update_n_text)

        # 5. Final Normal Curve (to be revealed)
        bell_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: np.exp(-(x**2) / (2 * 0.6**2)) * 1.2,
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color="#00FFFF"
        ).set_stroke(width=4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Central Limit Theorem reveals a hidden mathematical law.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.play(FadeIn(pop_group), FadeIn(main_axes_group))
        self.add(bars, n_display)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # As sample size grows, the distribution shape transforms.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(15), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Uniform or skewed data eventually yields a bell curve.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(30), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This normal distribution is symmetrical and highly predictable.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        self.play(Create(bell_curve), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Large samples always find order within the original mess.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        
        # Grand Reveal: Flash the Bell Curve
        self.play(
            bell_curve.animate.set_stroke(color=WHITE, width=8),
            run_time=0.4
        )
        self.play(
            bell_curve.animate.set_stroke(color="#00FFFF", width=5),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters for safety
        bars.remove_updater(update_histogram)
        n_val_text.remove_updater(update_n_text)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture script
        lecture_lines = [
            'The mean of averages equals the original population mean.', 
            'Larger samples create a much narrower and taller curve.', 
            'This increased precision reduces our overall margin of error.', 
            'Typically, a sample size of thirty is the magic number.', 
            'Mathematics provides certainty even when starting with chaos.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Pillars", lecture_lines)

        # --- Initialization ---
        # ValueTracker for the sample size n
        n_tracker = ValueTracker(4)
        mu_val = 0
        sigma_pop = 1.0

        # Axes: Located in the center-right area (B1 to F6)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3.5, 3.5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False},
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6")

        # Mu Center Highlight (#FFD700)
        mu_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(mu_val, 0), axes.c2p(mu_val, 4.5), 
            color="#FFD700", stroke_width=3
        )
        # FIXED: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX distribution dependency (FileNotFoundError: 'latex')
        mu_label = Text("μ", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        mu_label.next_to(mu_line, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Standard Error Formula (#FFFFFF)
        # FIXED: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX distribution dependency
        formula = Text("SE = σ / √n", color=WHITE, font_size=26)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Sample size indicator for the animation
        n_val_label = Text("n = ", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        n_val_num = DecimalNumber(n_tracker.get_value(), num_decimal_places=0, color=YELLOW, font_size=28, mob_class=Text)
        n_val_num.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(n_tracker.get_value()))
        n_display = VGroup(n_val_label, n_val_num).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(n_display, "A6", scale_factor=0.9)

        # Magic Number Text (#00FF00)
        magic_number_txt = Text("Magic Number: n ≥ 30", color="#00FF00", font_size=26)
        self.place_at_grid(magic_number_txt, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Dynamic Bell Curve function (using dynamic n via ValueTracker)
        def get_bell_curve():
            n = n_tracker.get_value()
            se = sigma_pop / np.sqrt(n)
            # Normal distribution probability density function
            return axes.plot(
                lambda x: (1 / (se * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu_val) / se) ** 2),
                color=BLUE,
                x_range=[-3.5, 3.5]
            )

        # Persistent mobject with redrawer
        curve = always_redraw(get_bell_curve)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 'The mean of averages equals the original population mean.'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(Create(mu_line), Write(mu_label))
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # 'Larger samples create a much narrower and taller curve.'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula), Write(n_display))
        # Animate n from 4 to 30
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(30), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 'This increased precision reduces our overall margin of error.'
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Animate n further to 100 to show extreme precision
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(100), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # 'Typically, a sample size of thirty is the magic number.'
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(magic_number_txt))
        self.play(Indicate(magic_number_txt, color="#00FF00", scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # 'Mathematics provides certainty even when starting with chaos.'
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Highlight mu and the stability of the center
        self.play(Indicate(mu_line, color="#FFD700"), Flash(mu_line.get_top(), color="#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Colors
        COLOR_1 = "#33CCFF" # Light Blue for Factory/Batteries
        COLOR_2 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow for Bell Curve
        COLOR_3 = "#FFFFFF" # White for Conclusion

        self.setup_layout(
            "Why It Matters: The Statistician's Superpower", 
            [
                "This theorem is a superpower for predicting population behavior.", 
                "Factories use it to guarantee product quality and safety.", 
                "We find order in complexity through the bell curve."
            ]
        )

        # Helper to create battery
        def create_battery(color=COLOR_1):
            body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.4, width=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            tip = Rectangle(height=0.06, width=0.1, color=color, fill_opacity=1).next_to(body, UP, buff=0)
            return VGroup(body, tip)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Factory setting: Conveyor belt and batteries
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        
        belt = Line(self.grid["E1"], self.grid["E6"], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
        belt_base = Line(self.grid["E1"] + DOWN*0.1, self.grid["E6"] + DOWN*0.1, color=GREY_E, stroke_width=2)
        factory_group = VGroup(belt, belt_base)
        
        # Batteries
        batteries = VGroup(*[create_battery() for _ in range(6)])
        for i, battery in enumerate(batteries):
            self.place_at_grid(battery, f"E{i+1}")
            battery.shift(UP * 0.3)

        self.play(Create(factory_group))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b, shift=RIGHT) for b in batteries], lag_ratio=0.2))
        
        # Battery movement loop simulation
        self.play(
            *[b.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.0) for b in batteries[:-1]],
            batteries[-1].animate.set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Bell Curve over small sample
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_2)
        
        # Highlight sample (center batteries)
        sample_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(batteries[2], batteries[3]), color=COLOR_2, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bell Curve
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3], 
            y_range=[0, 1], 
            x_length=4, 
            y_length=2.5, 
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY_D}
        )
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), color=COLOR_2)
        curve_label = Text("Normal Distribution", font_size=18, color=COLOR_2)
        curve_group = VGroup(axes, curve, curve_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(curve_group, "A2", "D5")

        self.play(Create(sample_rect))
        self.play(FadeIn(curve_group))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final conclusion text
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_3)
        
        conclusion_text = Text("Predicting the Unknown", font_size=36, color=COLOR_3, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_in_area(conclusion_text, "B2", "D5") # Centered in the right area
        
        # Transition to conclusion
        self.play(
            FadeOut(curve_group),
            FadeOut(factory_group),
            FadeOut(batteries),
            FadeOut(sample_rect),
            FadeIn(conclusion_text)
        )
        
        self.play(Indicate(conclusion_text, scale_factor=1.1, color=COLOR_3))
        self.wait(3)

        # Fade out all
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(conclusion_text))

outline.topic: Central Limit Theorem: The Magic of the Bell Curve
outline.target_audience: University students taking introductory statistics or data science

sections.title: The Mystery of Predictable Chaos
sections.content: Hook the audience by presenting a world of chaotic, non-normal data. Introduce the core question: How can we find order in a world where individual data points are unpredictable?
sections.example: Imagine a forest of 'Gigantic Squirrels' where some are tiny (1kg) and some are massive (20kg). Their weights don't follow a bell curve; it's a messy, flat distribution. If we pick one squirrel, we have no idea what it will weigh.

sections.title: Prerequisite Kit: Populations and Samples
sections.content: Define the 'Population' (everyone) vs. a 'Sample' (a small group). Explain the 'Sample Mean'—the average of one small group. Use visual overlays to show the difference between a single data point and an average.
sections.example: Visual: A large bag of multi-colored marbles (Population). One hand scoops out 5 marbles (Sample) and calculates their average weight (Sample Mean). Repeat this visually with different scoops.

sections.title: The Experiment: Gathering the Averages
sections.content: Introduce the 'Sampling Distribution'. This is the heart of CLT: instead of plotting individual squirrels, we plot the *averages* of many groups. Show an animation of a histogram being built one sample at a time.
sections.example: Chef Panda weighs 30 random squirrels and records the average. He does this 1,000 times. We watch a graph where each 'average' falls into a slot. Even though the squirrels are chaotic, the slots start forming a specific shape.

sections.title: The Grand Reveal: The Bell Curve Emerges
sections.content: Explain the CLT's core finding: As the sample size (n) increases, the distribution of sample means will look like a Normal Distribution (Bell Curve), regardless of the population's original shape.
sections.example: Animation: Start with a 'Uniform' (flat) or 'Skewed' (lopsided) distribution. Watch as the sample size grows from n=2 to n=30. The histogram 'melts' from a messy shape into a perfect, symmetrical Bell Curve.

sections.title: The Mathematical Pillars
sections.content: Detail the three critical properties: 1. The mean of sample means equals the population mean. 2. The spread (Standard Error) gets narrower as sample size increases. 3. The 'Magic Number' n ≥ 30 for most distributions.
sections.example: Graphical Formula: Show a Bell Curve narrowing and becoming taller as 'n' increases from 10 to 100, visually demonstrating that larger samples provide more certainty/precision.

sections.title: Why It Matters: The Statistician's Superpower
sections.content: Conclude with real-world applications. Because of CLT, we can make confident predictions about a whole population just by looking at a few samples, even if we don't know the 'shape' of the underlying population.
sections.example: Quality Control: A battery factory doesn't know the exact lifespan distribution of every battery, but by testing samples of 40, they can use the Bell Curve to predict the probability of a batch being defective.
